title: Travel in Kazakhstan: From the Steppe to the Mountains
paragraphs: Kazakhstan is the ninth-largest country in the world, and for Kazakhstani students this creates both an opportunity and a paradox: many of them have travelled to countries far away but have never explored their own. Amir, who studies computer science at WKU, admits that he visited Dubai before he visited Turkestan. "I had been abroad twice before I went to our own ancient city," he says. "I am not sure what that says about me, or about us."

The obstacles to domestic travel are real. Kazakhstan's vast distances mean that getting from Uralsk to Almaty is not a short trip — it takes over thirty hours by train, and flights, while faster, can be expensive for students. The railway network, which was largely built in the Soviet era, connects major cities but leaves smaller destinations difficult to reach without a car. Public transport within regions is limited, and rental cars require a licence and confidence that many students do not yet have.

Despite these challenges, domestic tourism in Kazakhstan is growing rapidly. Social media has played a significant role: images of Charyn Canyon — a vast, red-rock gorge in the south-east — have been shared so widely that it has become one of the most visited natural sites in Central Asia. The Burabay resort area, two hours from Nur-Sultan, fills with visitors every summer. The ancient Silk Road cities of Turkestan and Otrar attract students of history from across the country.

Zhibek, who is planning a trip to Shymkent this summer, explains her thinking: "Shymkent is close to Turkestan — I can visit the Yasawi Mausoleum in a day trip. The food in the south is different from what we eat in Uralsk. And it is cheaper than going abroad." She has booked her train tickets already. She is going to stay in a hostel and spend five days exploring the old city, the bazaars, and the nearby historical sites.

For students who want to travel further within Kazakhstan, the key is planning. The cheapest train tickets sell out weeks in advance. Accommodation in popular destinations fills up in July and August. Knowing this, experienced student travellers book months ahead, travel in shoulder seasons (May-June and September-October), and use overnight trains to save money on hotels.

What makes travel within Kazakhstan particularly rewarding is its variety. In a single trip, you can move from the open steppe — flat, silent, and seemingly endless — to rocky canyons, to pine-forested mountains, to cities that have stood for over a thousand years. The landscape changes faster than you expect, and the people change with it: each region has its own accent, its own food, and its own sense of identity.

The advice most Kazakhstani travellers give is simple: start with somewhere inside the country. Once you have seen Charyn Canyon at sunrise, or sat in the courtyard of the Yasawi Mausoleum, or watched the sun set over Lake Balkhash, you will understand something about this country that no classroom could teach you.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I've been thinking about planning a trip somewhere. Have you been anywhere in Kazakhstan?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I went to Almaty two years ago. This summer I'm going to Shymkent for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I want to see Charyn Canyon. I've seen so many photos — it looks incredible.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: You should go in May or September — not July. It's too hot in summer.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Good point. How do people usually get there? Is there a direct train?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: You fly to Almaty and then take a bus or taxi. It's about four hours from the city.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I'll look into it. Maybe we could go together in May?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I'd love that! Book early though — the tickets and hostels fill up fast.

vocab.example: Charyn Canyon has become one of the most visited destinations in Central Asia.

vocab.example: Accommodation in popular destinations fills up quickly in summer.
